favourite.heading: Why Western Michigan can pull away
bullets: Western Michigan is the better football team by 16.0 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (-16.0 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Western Michigan by 0.4 points: early-down offence vs early-down defence (-0.4 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Rice can keep it close
bullets: Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 4.6 points to Rice (+4.6 pts).
Playing at Rice is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -30.7 to p90 +13.3 for Rice, so a projection of -7.7 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
